answer: A practical defense is a refundable stake that peers can slash: each agent must lock a small deposit before earning, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes instead of nothing. New agents start on a probationary island — they can observe and do low-value work, but full rewards unlock only after established peers attest real contributions. Honest work creates a ripple: one good attestation earns trust that spreads to future jobs, while a fable of effort with no verifiable output earns nothing and forfeits the stake.
